transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (Redwood), Dr. Anika Rao (CTO, Rivermark), Marcus Bell (Head of Infra), Sofia Martinez (Security Lead), Diego Alvarez (DevOps)

Summary: Intro, goals and constraints, deep dive on networking options and security; agreed on next steps.

00:00:00 - Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um happy to kick off, is this time still good?
00:00:05 - Dr. Anika Rao: yes, thanks Maya, all good on our side.
00:00:12 - Maya Chen: cool quick agenda, we'll run through what Rivermark is trying to achieve, then Liam will go through architecture options for Private/VPC deployment, and we'll capture any blockers. expected outcome is alignment on network approach and what we need for a pilot. sound right?
00:00:30 - Marcus Bell: yep that sounds right, mainly concerned about cross-account peering and ip ranges. we have 3 aws accounts and a partner account that need to access inference endpoints.
00:00:45 - Liam O'Connor: perfect, i'll start by laying out the three common patterns we've seen: vpc peering, aws privatelink / endpoints (interface endpoints), and transit-gateway / vpn. each has tradeoffs around ip routing, security, and peering limits.
00:01:10 - Liam O'Connor: with vpc peering you get direct private routing but you can't transitive route - so if you peer A->B and B->C that doesn't automatically peer A->C. also cidr overlap is a hard blocker.
00:01:30 - Diego Alvarez: we already have overlapping cidrs between two accounts, we try to avoid re-netting, so peering might be tough.
00:01:40 - Sofia Martinez: also from security we want no public egress for traffic that goes to the model endpoints; we need traffic to stay in-region and be subject to our inspection/ids.
00:01:55 - Marcus Bell: what about privatelink? i thought that avoids cidr overlap issues, right?
00:02:05 - Liam O'Connor: yes interface endpoints are one-way, they create ENIs in your VPC and you route to them; they avoid cidr overlap but are regional and can be per-account. PrivateLink works well when you want stable single-hostnames and avoid peering. downside is it requires ENIs and you pay per endpoint/hour + data processing.
00:02:35 - Olivia Park: to add, with PrivateLink you can centrally expose the service from Redwood to many customer accounts without peering, and we support VPC endpoint DNS overrides so your apps resolve the private hostname.
00:02:50 - Dr. Anika Rao: ok, cost is a factor for us but security and no overlap are higher priority. we also have a compliance requirement that keys stay in our KMS. can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest?
00:03:10 - Maya Chen: yes we support KMS integration options for Private deployments — we can either use customer-managed keys for certain storage layers or work with an HSM if required; Liam can share the exact pattern we recommend.
00:03:23 - Liam O'Connor: for the private offering we support bringing your key via KMS grants and cross-account roles so the customer retains key control. there are some IAM setup steps but we've done this with other healthcare customers.
00:03:40 - Sofia Martinez: good to hear. what about audit logs and retention, we need to keep request logs for 7 years per policy. is that supported?
00:03:50 - Maya Chen: we export audit logs to your s3/stack and can ship with a retention policy, and we support forwarding to your SIEM via Kinesis or direct ingestion. i'll attach our logging/retention doc.
00:04:10 - Marcus Bell: network wise we also have to deal with an egress firewall that inspects TLS. can we route traffic to an internal proxy?
00:04:22 - Liam O'Connor: yes, we have two patterns: 1) keep all egress in your VPC - if you use PrivateLink the traffic terminates in your VPC so your proxy can inspect, or 2) if you peer to a Redwood-managed VPC for Dedicated, you'd need to allow a small set of egress IPs and handle peering route tables; that's less ideal for your no-public-egress policy.
00:04:47 - Diego Alvarez: what about multi-region models? we operate in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 and need data residency for EU traffic. can Redwood place Private endpoints in region?
00:04:59 - Olivia Park: absolutely, we can deploy regionally — Private endpoints are regional, and we recommend deploying an endpoint in each region where you have strict residency. we then route traffic to the nearest endpoint.
00:05:20 - Marcus Bell: cross-region peering is messy, and transit-gateway costs add up. i guess PrivateLink per region might be simpler even if it's more operational work.
00:05:28 - Liam O'Connor: agreed, PrivateLink scales well across accounts and regions but you will manage multiple endpoints. another option is a transit-gateway with central inspection VPC, but that requires non-overlapping CIDRs and more architecture work.
00:05:45 - Dr. Anika Rao: can Redwood handle the DNS mapping? we have service discovery expectations where hostname resolves internally to the private endpoint.
00:05:55 - Olivia Park: yes we support private DNS for the endpoint so the Redwood hostnames resolve to your endpoint ENIs. we can also provide split-horizon DNS instructions if you need different behavior for on-prem vs cloud.
00:06:12 - Sofia Martinez: about identity and access, we use SAML SSO and have strict RBAC. integration possible?
00:06:18 - Maya Chen: yes we support SSO (SAML/OIDC) and can integrate with your IdP for admin access. for API keys and service roles, we recommend short-lived credentials and can integrate with your identity broker.
00:06:33 - Marcus Bell: one more thing: our infra team requires the ability to run internal performance benchmarks. what does Redwood recommend for benchmarking latency and throughput for a pilot?
00:06:45 - Liam O'Connor: for pilot we typically provision a small dedicated capacity in the region or a Private deployment in your VPC with minimal nodes; then we run controlled load tests with your prompt set. we'll instrument p95/p99 latency and token throughput. recommended window is 2-4 hours with ramp.
00:07:05 - Diego Alvarez: do you have tooling or scripts we can run?
00:07:09 - Liam O'Connor: yes we'll provide a loadgen script and a sample benchmark sheet.
00:07:18 - Dr. Anika Rao: great. question on failover — if a region is down do you do cross-region fallback?
00:07:26 - Olivia Park: our smart routing can fallback to a compatible model in another region but for Private deployments we coordinate region-level failover with the customer since networking + compliance may prevent automatic cross-region traffic. we can implement a controlled fallback pattern though.
00:07:44 - Sofia Martinez: we will need SLA and clear uptime numbers for any pilot.
00:07:50 - Maya Chen: we provide SLA options for Dedicated and Private deployments; i'll include SLA targets in the packet.
00:08:00 - Marcus Bell: another network detail — we use strict /24 allocations per team, we're worried about IP exhaustion with ENIs created by endpoints. how many ENIs are needed?
00:08:12 - Liam O'Connor: PrivateLink creates one ENI per AZ per endpoint. so for three AZs you'll see three ENIs per account per endpoint, and each ENI consumes IPs from your subnet. if you have small /24s you might need to carve a slightly larger subnet or use dedicated subnets for endpoints. we'll include the sizing guidance.
00:08:35 - Diego Alvarez: ok makes sense.
00:08:40 - Maya Chen: any blockers on the security side?
00:08:43 - Sofia Martinez: we need to confirm data access patterns: are logs containing PII by default? how are they redacted?
00:08:51 - Olivia Park: logs can include request ids and non-sensitive metadata. we can configure masking/redaction for payloads and support customer-managed log sinks so sensitive data never leaves your control.
00:09:05 - Marcus Bell: for the pilot timeline, we're aiming for an internal sign-off by end of May, so pilot in early June if we can get the network details in next week.
00:09:15 - Maya Chen: reasonable. we'll try to get the packet over by Friday and Liam will follow up with the diagram.
00:09:23 - Liam O'Connor: i'll also put together recommended IAM role snippets and example security-group rules.
00:09:32 - Dr. Anika Rao: thanks — quick question on pricing: is Private deployment per-node monthly or usage?
00:09:38 - Maya Chen: Private is typically a hybrid: a base infra fee (reserved/dedicated capacity) plus usage-based tokens. for small pilot we can do a short-term reserved node with usage credits. i'll include 3 options in the estimate.
00:09:52 - Diego Alvarez: are there known performance differences between Private and Hosted?
00:09:58 - Liam O'Connor: performance is comparable when deployed in-region; Private gives you more deterministic network path and isolation. the main differences are operational control and sometimes lower variance on p99 latency.
00:10:12 - Marcus Bell: ok that's helpful.
00:10:15 - Maya Chen: any more questions?
00:10:18 - Marcus Bell: one more on compliance — do you support customer-managed audit trails and immutable logs?
00:10:24 - Olivia Park: yes we can ship immutable logs to your S3 with object lock and retention policies, and we support pushing to your log archive.
00:10:35 - Sofia Martinez: thanks.
00:10:37 - Maya Chen: quick recap and action items: we'll send pricing and security docs, liam will send network diagram and IAM snippets, customer shares cidrs and region constraints. schedule the SE benchmark for the week of 4/27. does that line up?
00:10:55 - Dr. Anika Rao: yes that works.
00:11:00 - Maya Chen: awesome thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing.
00:11:05 - (small chitchat and meeting wrap)
00:11:20 - End of recorded portion — note: call continued for private follow-up between Liam and Marcus about exact subnet sizes (unrecorded)
